correctness.rationale: The de Bruijn representation has incidence rank 3 and one independent total constraint, leaving four flow dimensions. Each of 13 distinct endpoint divergences has asymptotic unrestricted count \(m^4/288+O(m^3)\). The balanced series is exactly \(\frac{1+z^3}{(1-z)^2(1-z^2)(1-z^3)(1-z^4)}\), yielding \(m^4/288+O(m^3)\); adding two-edge paths sandwiches other sectors. Disconnected supports lie in a union of eight codimension-at-least-one boundary faces because a strictly positive solution exists for large m, hence at most O(m^3). Exact independent computational set comparisons pass for n=3..15 and balanced coefficient checks for m=0..60. Computations are only corroborative, not proof.

originality.rationale: The strongest accessible original sources were inspected at their relevant theorem and higher-order sections. The 2004 Markov analysis gives class multiplicities and redundancy, not the number of distinct linear order-two types. The 2009/2010 first-order cyclic Markov enumeration concerns complete transition graphs and omits sparse binary second-order endpoints. Gabrys and Milenkovic give a general multispectrum code framework without the fixed three-mer capacity constant. The closest indexed result is for two-mers, not three-mers. No checked primary theorem states or implies the rational balanced-flow series and thirteen-sector coefficient. Standard counting methods themselves are not claimed as original.
residual_risks: An unindexed enumeration under second-order empirical distributions, flow polytopes, or de Bruijn Markov types might already give 13/288.
General Ehrhart/flow counting frameworks could imply the coefficient after a nontrivial specialization, but no checked theorem provides the specialization outright.
A self-review does not replace external mathematical peer review.

value.rationale: \(Q_3(n)\) is the precise natural maximum size of a binary linear length-three read-spectrum reconstruction code. Its quartic growth and sharp coefficient \(13/288\) distinguish feasible sparse Markov types from unconstrained eight-component compositions and reflect twelve additional boundary endpoint sectors. A general lower-order formula is not required for this practically motivated fixed-read invariant.
